subject: Post-demo qualification: p95/p99 end-to-end latency targets & hosted vs incumbent
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: p95/p99 targets + next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on qualification criteria before any pilot: 

Summary of what I heard on the call:
- Target e2e p95: 200ms for short prompts (<= 64 tokens), p99: 420ms.
- Sustained concurrent throughput target: ~250 qps during peak, with 1k burst headroom.
- Streaming: client expects token-by-token three-way streaming (server -> client -> frontend) with max per-token latency budget of 35ms after model token decode starts.
- Acceptance includes cold-start behavior, KV-cache warm paths, and end-to-end network hops (client -> CDN -> API -> model).

Proposed qualification plan:
1) Share your incumbent empirical p95/p99 traces (we discussed sample CSV) — thanks for that export.
2) Redwood will run two quick experiments in our hosted staging:
   a) 5-minute smoke load at 100 qps for short prompts (measure p50/p95/p99)
   b) 30-minute sustained run at 250 qps with 1s-5s prompt variability to exercise batching and tail latency.
3) Streaming check: we will run streaming sessions (10 concurrent streams, 5-minute each) to measure token-latency and reassembly on the client.
4) Define pass/fail: p95 <= 200ms and p99 <= 450ms (initial relaxed p99 to account for cold starts) for hosted staging.

Next steps that I need from you by EOD Wednesday:
- Confirm those target numbers are still accurate for Acme.
- Attach the incumbent traces (CSV), sample request shapes, and any client-side instrumentation you can share.
- Point of contact for SRE coordination (we may need an IP allowlist).

I’ve attached a short test-plan draft and our hosted SLO proposal. Looping Grace (CS) for timeline/ops and Markus for engineering coordination.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: p95/p99 targets + next steps

Hi Vanessa — great notes, thanks. I attached the CSV sample ("acme-current-provider-latency-sample-20261109.csv"). A few clarifications from our side: 

- The live numbers we shared are measured client-side (end-to-end including our front-end deserialization). The provider-side APM shows p99s closer to ~300ms, but the extra hop in our app inflates the end-to-end tail.
- For streaming, our mobile app needs per-token delivery under 50ms for a smooth UX; desktop tolerates slightly higher.
- Peak concurrency expectation: our current peak path sees 220 sustained qps for the main recommendation endpoint and occasional 800 qps bursts for onboarding flows.

SRE contact: Luis Moreno (luis.moreno@acme-ai.com) — he can provide IPs for allowlist and a short VPN window if needed.

We can confirm targets: p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 420ms would be acceptable if you can show consistent warm-cache behavior and predictable degradation strategy (fallback model/region).

I attached the CSV and a short note on client instrumentation. Happy to schedule the first smoke test this week if you can slot it.

—Elena
Director of Product, Acme AI
Attachments: acme-current-provider-latency-sample-20261109.csv

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 16:02:10 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: p95/p99 targets + next steps

Thanks Elena — got the CSV and the instrumentation notes. Rishi and Markus — can you confirm the quick-hosted test variations below and whether we can meet Acme's target envelope? I added Grace for rollout/timing.

Proposed quick tests (hosted staging):
- Smoke (5 min): 100 qps, short prompts (<=64 tokens), measure p50/p95/p99.
- Sustained (30 min): 250 qps steady, variable prompt lengths (64-512 tokens) to stress batching and KV cache.
- Burst window (10 min): step to 800 qps for 2x 1-minute bursts to observe graceful degradation.
- Streaming sessions: 10 concurrent streams, 300 tokens total, measure per-token latency distribution and reassembly delay on our side.

Acceptance criteria we will validate in-hosted:
- p95 <= 200ms for short prompts (warm), p99 <= 420ms (warm).
- Token-level streaming median <= 18ms, 95th <= 45ms on our hosted path.
- No unrecoverable errors at 800 qps bursts — errors should follow a documented fallback (queue/backpressure) and be transparent in logs.

Timeline: if SRE can provide allowlist by tomorrow EOD, Rishi can run smoke tests Wed morning and share a results packet by Wed 1pm PST. If all good, we propose a 2-week pilot with a 10% traffic shift.

Markus / Rishi — can you comment on tooling we will provide for them (trace ids, realtime dashboard links) and whether we need any special IAM/KMS coordination for traces?

Vanessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: p95/p99 targets + next steps

Quick internal sync — plan confirmed:
- I will spin the smoke and sustained runs in hosted-staging tomorrow morning. I expect to capture: p50/p95/p99, token-level histograms, queue depths, batch sizes, and per-instance GPU utilization.
- For streaming, we'll run with both server-sent-events (SSE) and gRPC-streaming emulation to mirror Acme's mobile client behavior; we'll collect reassembly and jitter stats.
- We will publish a realtime dashboard (link will be shared in the results packet) and include trace ids. No KMS changes required for staging; for pilot we will request an allowlist and temporary certs if Acme wants TLS client auth.

I will attach a short results summary and the raw CSVs to the HubSpot deal (HUB-52341-Acme) after the run. If we see p99 > 450ms we should be ready to propose a quantized model variant / reduced batching fallback to hit tail targets.

—Rishi
